To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the spin distribution of millisecond pulsar is largely determined by their mass-accretion histories, (ii) millisecond pulsars are typically born as low-mass neutron stars, (iii) the true ages of millisecond pulsaries are typically much older than the ages inferred from their spin parameters, (iv) the spin evolution of recycled pulsars is not uniquely determined by their mass accretion, but also depends on the amount of angular momentum that they have retained after their birth,
the spin distribution of binary millisecond radio pulsars can be explained by their formation in IMXBs and LMXBs, and that their true ages are significantly smaller than their characteristic ages.

the recycling of pulsar via RLO in IMXBs and LMXBs leads to a spin-up process that is characterized by different amounts of accreted matter, different mass loss rates during RLO, and a different amount of rotational energy lost during the RLO phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spin evolution of recycled pulsars and the formation of millisecond pulsar systems with different types of companion stars.
the evolution of millisecond pulsar binaries and their formation in close binary systems.
the formation and evolution of binary millisecond radio pulsars with CO and He WD companions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of binary MSPs with CO WDs and He WDs is not a unique process and that both scenarios are possible.
the formation of recycled pulsars is a multi-stage process and that their spin periods are not a reliable indicator of their true ages.
the formation of millisecond pulsar systems with CO WD companions is not possible in LMXBs, but can be achieved in IMXBs, whereas systems with He WD companions can form in LMXBs and IMXBs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the recycling process in LMXBs is more effective in spin-up than in IMXBs because the accreted mass in LMXBs (≲0.1 M⊙) is larger and because the pulsars in LXMBS are typically more massive and have larger magnetic fields.
the spin-up process of millisecond pulsar is very complex and depends on the details of the accretion process.
recycled pulsars are mainly formed in LMXBs, with the spin-up process being dominated by the Roche-love decoupling phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the spin-up of pulsars in IMXBs is a much faster process than in LMXBs and that the observed spin distributions of recycled millisecond pulsars can be understood in terms of the different types of companion stars.
the recycling mechanism in LMXBs and IMXBs leads to different types of millisecond pulsar companions and different spin distributions.

the formation history of a pulsar can be reconstructed by comparing its true age and spin period to the spin-up track of a pulsar in a binary system, and that the recycling process can be used as a powerful tool for understanding binary evolution.
